To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim

The Seller's preamble says these positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." **We should not accept that.**

- Our playbook allows the 20% cap and the 18-month period only with **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft**. No such authority has been given.
- A statement in the other side's covering note cannot stand in for that authority.
- Almost every other position in the package goes beyond even our fallbacks. These include thresholds, fundamentals, fraud, disclosure and buyer knowledge. Nothing in our playbook would allow those to be "settled."

**Action:** Before the mark-up goes out, confirm directly with Amelia Frost whether she has agreed anything with Harbourglass. Our mark-up should state that no positions are agreed until documented and approved by Wattlebridge.

The "market context" figures (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are the Seller's advocacy. They are not a benchmark we are bound by.

---

## Material issues, in priority order

### 1. Fraud carve-out removed (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5, and cl. 12.3)
**Seller:** The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature." Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."

**Why it matters:** Read together, these would extend the caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Clause 12.3 also works as a hidden general override. It would pull the Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific-indemnity and covenant claims into the general regime unless each is carved out expressly.

**Push back:**
- Add an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-negotiable, and no one on our side can waive it.
- Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" formulation. Limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims, and only where expressly stated.

### 2. Title and capacity folded into the general regime
**Seller:** Title and capacity warranties take the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."

**Why it matters:** We are buying 100% of the shares. A title defect goes to the whole price, so a AUD 4.8m cap on title is plainly inadequate.

**Push back:** Reject. Fundamental and Title claims need a separate regime:
- 100% cap (AUD 24m);
- at least six years;
- outside the general de minimis, basket and any knowledge bar.

### 3. General cap of 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1)
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written authority. We do not have it.

**Push back:** Restate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not offer or signal 20% unless and until written authority is obtained for this draft.

### 4. Thresholds (cl. 12.2)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 (about 1% of price) | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Excess only (deductible) | Tipping: first dollar once exceeded |

**Why it matters:** The combination of a 5x higher basket and a deductible structure means the first AUD 250k of valid loss is never recoverable. The higher de minimis also excludes claims below AUD 25k from counting toward the basket at all.

**Push back:** AUD 5,000 de minimis, and an AUD 50,000 tipping basket with recovery from the first dollar.

### 5. General claims period of 18 months (cl. 12.3 / 13)
**Playbook:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval. We do not have it.

**Why it matters:** 24 months gives us two full audit cycles after Completion.

**Push back:** Restate 24 months. As noted in issue 1, the time limit must not extend to fraud, Title, Tax, IP, indemnities or covenants.

### 6. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])
**Seller:** Discloses the entire data room as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."

**Why it matters:** This deems everything in a large data room and in public records to qualify every warranty, which largely hollows out the warranties.

Two further points:
- The cut-off is 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Any later uploads must not be swept in.
- [1.4] (no admission of breach or materiality) is broadly acceptable. It must not, however, operate to dilute specific disclosures or our indemnities.

**Push back:**
- Delete [1.1] and [1.2].
- Only specific disclosures against identified warranties count, and only where they are fair, meaning sufficient detail for the Buyer to assess the nature and scope of the matter.
- No disclosure against Fundamental/Title warranties or specific indemnities.

### 7. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl. 8.3)
**Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Why it matters:** This is a blanket exclusion based on imputed and constructive knowledge. It would undermine claims on matters we specifically diligenced and priced, such as Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006.

**Push back:** Delete it. If any qualifier survives, it must:
- be limited to **seller** knowledge;
- name specific seller knowledge persons;
- include a reasonable-enquiry standard;
- never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

**Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms:**
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or about 30% of FY26 revenue;
- consent under cl. 11.2 is subject to conditions in cl. 11.3;
- no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied has been provided.

**Why it matters:** "Satisfied on delivery" could let Completion occur on a consent that is conditional or not yet effective. That puts 30% of revenue at risk. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size.

**Push back:** The condition precedent should require **effective, unconditional consent (or consent with all cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied), with documentary evidence, delivered before Completion.** Strengthen the Seller's obligation beyond reasonable endeavours. Our Completion deliverables checklist should include the executed consent plus evidence for each cl. 11.3 condition.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7)
**Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be "addressed by a release provided following Completion." Disclosure item 3 confirms it has not been repaid and there is no discharge.

**Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free. If we complete before the security is discharged, the Company's assets (and possibly the shares) remain encumbered and change-control under cl. 8.1 may be triggered. A vague post-Completion release gives us no enforceable comfort.

**Push back:**
- Require a current payout letter from Riverlark.
- Repayment should be made directly from Completion funds to Riverlark.
- Executed security releases and PPSR discharges (or deeds of release with irrevocable lodgement authority) should be delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval.

### 10. DD-005 bonuses excluded from the funds flow
**Seller:** The AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. Disclosure item 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.

**Why it matters:** These are Company liabilities triggered by Completion. If they are not in the funds flow or deducted from price, the Buyer funds them through the Company after Completion. The on-costs are unquantified and are an additional liability.

**Push back:** Do one of the following:
- add the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding mechanics) as a specific line item in the funds flow, paid through payroll; or
- treat them as Seller-funded or debt-like, with a matching price adjustment.

In either case, back this with a specific indemnity for any shortfall.

### 11. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl. 11.1)
**Seller:** The indemnity covers only the specific SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."

**Disclosure item 4:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but this is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

**Why it matters:** The real risk is that the Company does not own the SOW3 IP, together with any third-party claims and remediation costs. The payment amount alone is not the risk. We should not assume either way that the AUD 180k is owed or paid.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to, or claims concerning, Ironquay/SOW3 Project Materials.
- Keep the SOW3 cure mechanism: verified payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable.
- Ask for bank evidence of the payment status.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sch. 6)
**Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."

**Disclosure item 6:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address, potentially covering about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are unknown.

**Our position:** We should not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or dollar figure, because the record does not support any of those.

**Push back:**
- Add covenants to preserve all logs and evidence.
- Require the Seller to complete a proper investigation, including an assessment of any notification obligations, and provide regular written updates before Completion.
- Give the Buyer consultation rights on any regulator or individual communications.
- Exclude the matter from general disclosure.
- Consider a specific, uncapped-by-the-general-regime indemnity for losses arising from the incident. We should frame this neutrally, without a numeric amount.

### 13. Tax / IP said to be "settled under the general regime"
**Playbook:** These terms remain **open**. Nothing has been resolved, and we should not assume unlimited liability either.

**Push back:** Reject the characterisation. State expressly that the Tax and IP warranty and indemnity terms remain under negotiation. Keep Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories as separate regimes, not subsumed into the general cap.

### 14. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's own share register.

**Disclosure item 10:** The Seller itself concedes this only identifies its source and is not Buyer verification.

**Why it matters:** An internal register is self-serving.

**Push back:** Require independent evidence before Completion:
- ASIC company extract;
- share issue and transfer history with supporting resolutions and stamping;
- PPSR searches over the shares;
- evidence of the Seller's corporate authority and capacity (board approvals, constitution);
- confirmation that there are no options, convertibles or encumbrances.

---

## Secondary items (verify, low priority)

- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000):** The Seller calls them ordinary course, and the disclosure is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Per playbook, we **assess** them: review DD-008/DD-011 for timing, terminability and accrual. Do not reflexively treat them as Debt or deduct them from price. Decide once the facts are known.
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The disclosure says notification only (lease) and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale (Mossvale). Confirm both by reviewing the clauses directly. If they are confirmed, the lease notification becomes a Completion mechanic.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Do not treat anything as agreed.** Confirm with Amelia Frost before sending the mark-up, and make clear that no positions are final.
2. **Reinsert the fraud carve-out** across all limitations, and **delete the "all Claims" overrides** (cl. 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5).
3. **Restore a separate Fundamental/Title regime**: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Cap 25% / AUD 6m; claims period 24 months.** Hold the fallbacks of 20% and 18 months, which are not authorised.
5. **Thresholds:** AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k tipping basket recoverable from the first dollar.
6. **Disclosure:** delete general data-room and public-record disclosure; specific fair disclosure only.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl. 8.3. Any fallback must use named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and never cover title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion. Reject "satisfied on delivery" and a bare reasonable-endeavours obligation.
9. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure (verified payment plus confirmatory assignment), and get bank evidence.
12. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants, and consider a neutral specific indemnity. Neither overstate nor understate the incident.
13. **Tax/IP:** expressly open, in separate regimes.
14. **Title:** independent ASIC, PPSR and authority evidence, not just DD-012.
15. **Sandbar, Lease, Mossvale:** diligence and verify; no automatic price consequence.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list for sending to Seller counsel. That version would leave out our internal fallback positions and the references to Amelia Frost's authority.

### 11. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl. 11.1)
